raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Thanks @leejnau for the pointer - the `retries: 2` one-liner this PR started with is superseded now that #46028 landed `retries: 3` on the same step. That alone doesn't close the gap though: the plugin's backoff adds up to about 15 s while each 502 took about 10.7 s to arrive on 10-30, so a run of 502s can still exhaust the retries, and any error that survives them is thrown out of `fetchJobs()` and ends the polling loop, failing the gate. A fresh occurrence landed in #42752 on 11-03 - a 502 from the jobs API that survived octokit's 3 retries at attempt 199 while polling stage B and killed the gate (run 41452221893).

## Modifications

I've pivoted the branch to the per-poll catch design leejnau suggested, rebuilt on current main. The polling loop now catches jobs-API errors per poll, logs a warning with the poll number and consecutive-failure count, and tries again at the next interval; the gate fails only after 3 consecutive failed polls, since this step only waits on other jobs and one missed poll costs nothing. The failure message names the tracker row (I1 in #42752) so future occurrences are easy to match. The step-level `retries: 3` from #46028 stays as the per-request retry layer, and the 304/ETag cached path and the completion detection are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - CI infrastructure only, no model or runtime code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A.

## Checklist

- [x] Format - the modified YAML re-parses and the inline script passes a syntax check; ran a local mock harness over the polling loop (transient 502s, consecutive failures, counter reset, 304/ETag path, deadline)
- [x] Unit tests - N/A; retry behavior verified locally via the harness
- [ ] Documentation - N/A for a CI action change
- [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks - N/A
- [x] Code style - follows the script's existing setFailed/console.log conventions

CI won't trigger on its own for this PR, so it would need a `/tag-run-ci-label` from someone authorized when there's a chance to look.

**PR title** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39549621158))
> PR title must use "[Type] scope: title" or "[Type] [Hardware] scope: title". Type must be one of: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, Chore. Scope is required and may be any module or model name, with unrestricted letter case (letters, numbers, dots, underscores, slashes, or hyphens). Hardware is optional; use a single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

Could someone add the `run-ci` label when they get a chance? There are two other open attempts on #42752 and it would help to have all of them actually testable — happy to close this in favor of a different direction if the maintainers prefer one of the others.

/tag-run-ci-label

Adding `run-ci` as requested above. Data from #46926: `wait-for-base-b` died on a jobs-API 5xx (`HttpError: Server Error` or `terminated`) in 7 attempts across three pr-test runs on 10-29 and 10-30 (runs 40871280279, 40987455545 and 41074304323), and in 3 more on an earlier run, 40628169090. Each time the gate went down, base-c was skipped and the attempt had to be rerun.

On those runs `GET /actions/runs/{id}/jobs` took 9–10.8 s per call, and on 10-30 three calls in a row returned 502 after about 10.7 s. `retries: 2` should cover isolated blips; it may not cover a sustained slow stretch like that one.

Thanks for running that and for the data — the sustained 502 stretch is a good catch. I kept retries: 2 to match what check-maintenance already ships, but happy to bump it if the slow stretches turn out to be common. One note: the label alone won't retrigger the base run since pr-test only fires on pushes — a /rerun-failed-ci would do it whenever convenient.

Heads-up: main already has this. #46028 (merged 10-31) added `retries: 3` to the same `actions/github-script` step in `.github/actions/wait-for-jobs/action.yml`, as a one-line rider (03a27e2a17). That's why this PR now shows as conflicting, and once rebased it would add nothing.

If you want a follow-up, the gap from the 10-30 data is still open: any error that survives the retries is thrown out of `fetchJobs()` and ends the polling loop, which fails the gate. The plugin's backoff adds up to about 15 s, and on 10-30 each 502 took about 10.7 s to arrive, so a run of 502s like that one can still exhaust `retries: 3`. Because the step only waits on other jobs, a sturdier option is to catch the error per poll, log it, and try again at the next interval, failing only after N consecutive failed polls. One missed poll costs nothing. Happy to review if you go that way; otherwise this one can probably be closed.
